reference_sql:
SELECT s.store_type, ROUND(AVG(t.order_eur), 2) AS avg_order_eur
FROM (
  -- one row per order
  SELECT order_id, store_code, SUM(net_revenue_eur) AS order_eur
  FROM sales
  GROUP BY order_id, store_code
) AS t
JOIN stores s ON s.store_code = t.store_code
GROUP BY s.store_type
alternatives:
SELECT s.store_type, ROUND(SUM(sa.net_revenue_eur) / COUNT(DISTINCT sa.order_id), 2) AS avg_order_eur
FROM sales sa
JOIN stores s ON s.store_code = sa.store_code
GROUP BY s.store_type

WITH order_values AS (
  -- one row per order
  SELECT order_id, store_code, SUM(net_revenue_eur) AS order_eur
  FROM sales
  GROUP BY order_id, store_code
)
SELECT s.store_type, ROUND(AVG(v.order_eur), 2) AS avg_order_eur
FROM order_values v
JOIN stores s ON s.store_code = v.store_code
GROUP BY s.store_type

other_way.sql:
SELECT s.store_type, ROUND(SUM(sa.net_revenue_eur) / COUNT(DISTINCT sa.order_id), 2) AS avg_order_eur
FROM sales sa
JOIN stores s ON s.store_code = sa.store_code
GROUP BY s.store_type
other_way.tradeoff: Total revenue over the count of distinct orders needs no inner step, but hides the order grain the average stands on.
